parsed.why: Sodomy law on the books, mob killing of a gender-nonconforming teen left unsolved, identity-targeted prison violence, and police saying they cannot protect LGBT residents. No documented border or document exposure, and resorts are described as insulated.

Death penalty for aggravated same-sex conduct, enforced arrests and shelter raids, a trans woman mobbed into a coma, digital entrapment, and state officials inciting attacks. Severe, enforced, state-directed targeting.

Hate-crime law covers gender identity and legal gender registration exists, but enforcement is uneven, under-reporting is documented, and customs and police searches of trans persons raise friction. Travel guide says the country widely accepts LGBTQ visitors.

Self-determination gender law, strong hate-crime and anti-discrimination protections, and open marriage. Offsetting this, dating-app ambush violence is rising and equality bodies document high assault rates. Regional procedural conflict is minor.

Gender-affirming surgery is criminalised for trans people with up to 10 years' imprisonment, and trans people cannot change markers. Morality and cybercrime laws are used against LGBT people, activists face coerced closures, and 93% of the public disapprove.
